title: Use the vehicle's recommended tyre pressure
content: The correct tyre pressure is the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation shown on the driver's door-area tyre label or in the owner's manual. The pressure printed on the tyre sidewall is not the vehicle's recommended operating pressure.
source_scope: General safety guidance; verify the specific vehicle manual.

title: Check tyre pressure when tyres are cold
content: Check all tyres, including the spare, at least monthly and before long trips. For a reliable reading, check when the vehicle has been parked for about three hours or before significant driving.

title: TPMS does not replace manual checks
content: A tyre-pressure monitoring warning may appear only after a tyre is already significantly underinflated. Drivers should still carry out regular pressure checks with a suitable gauge.

title: Inspect tread and wear indicators
content: Inspect tyre tread at least monthly. A tyre should be replaced when its tread is level with the built-in wear indicators. NHTSA also identifies 2/32 inch as an unsafe tread depth; this is safety guidance and should not be presented as Nigerian law.
source_scope: United States safety guidance; do not describe the threshold as Nigerian law.

title: Confirm the correct tyre size from the vehicle
content: Replacement tyres should match the original size or another size approved by the vehicle manufacturer. Confirm the size on the driver's door-area tyre label or in the owner's manual and consult a tyre professional when uncertain.
source_scope: General safety guidance; exact fitment is vehicle-specific.

title: Vibration can justify a balance inspection
content: Wheel balancing helps wheels rotate without causing shaking or vibration. New tyres should be balanced during installation. Persistent vibration can have more than one cause, so it should trigger inspection rather than a definite diagnosis.
source_scope: General safety guidance; physical inspection is required for diagnosis.

title: Pulling and uneven wear can justify alignment inspection
content: Correct wheel alignment supports tyre life and straight-line tracking. If a vehicle pulls on a straight, level road or shows uneven tyre wear, a qualified technician should inspect the alignment and related components.
source_scope: General guidance; pulling may have other causes.

title: Follow the vehicle's tyre-rotation guidance
content: Tyre rotation can reduce irregular wear. Use the interval and pattern in the owner's manual because some vehicles have different front and rear tyre sizes or other restrictions that make ordinary rotation unsuitable.
source_scope: General safety guidance; vehicle-specific instructions take priority.

title: A general rotation range is not a universal schedule
content: Where the manufacturer recommends rotation, NHTSA gives a general range of 5,000 to 8,000 miles and advises earlier attention when uneven wear appears. The owner's manual remains the controlling source for a specific vehicle.
source_scope: General range only; convert units if helpful and verify the manual.

title: Oil-change intervals vary by vehicle and oil
content: There is no safe universal oil-change interval. Engine design, oil specification, use conditions and manufacturer requirements differ, so the assistant should ask for the vehicle details and direct the user to the owner's manual or approved service schedule.
source_scope: Manufacturer guidance illustrating why intervals vary; not a schedule for every vehicle.

title: Use the manufacturer-specified fluids and fuel
content: The owner's manual is the primary source for the required engine oil, coolant, fuel octane and other vehicle-specific fluids. A higher grade or different fluid is not automatically better and should not be recommended without verifying the specification.
source_scope: Manufacturer guidance; verify each vehicle's manual.

title: Brake noise requires inspection
content: Squeaking or grinding can indicate brake-pad or related brake-system wear. The assistant must not confirm the cause remotely; it should recommend prompt inspection, especially when noise is accompanied by reduced braking, pulling, vibration or a warning light.
source_scope: General maintenance guidance; braking performance problems are safety-critical.

title: Stop safely when the engine is overheating
content: If the coolant-temperature warning indicates overheating or the gauge reaches the hot zone, stop the vehicle in a safe place. Allow the engine to cool and follow the owner's manual; do not continue driving or open a hot cooling system based only on chatbot instructions.
source_scope: General emergency guidance; exact warning displays and procedures are vehicle-specific.

title: The owner's manual controls scheduled maintenance
content: Scheduled maintenance depends on vehicle make, model, year, engine, mileage and operating conditions. The assistant should not invent an interval; it should request enough vehicle information and use the applicable owner's or maintenance manual.
source_scope: Manufacturer manual portal; use the correct vehicle document.

title: Visible tyre damage needs professional assessment
content: Bulges, cuts, cracks, exposed material or unusual deformation can signal unsafe tyre damage. Recommend avoiding unnecessary driving and obtaining professional inspection; a text conversation cannot determine whether a damaged tyre is safe.
source_scope: Manufacturer safety guidance; physical inspection is required.

title: Symptoms are not confirmed diagnoses
content: Vehicle symptoms such as vibration, pulling, warning lights or unusual noise may have several causes. The assistant may explain reasonable checks supported by sources, but it must label them as possibilities and recommend inspection before repair decisions.
source_scope: Project safety rule derived from the source-grounded decision-support scope.
